replacements.text: The acceptance-criteria standard has a coverage rule. It asks whether a commitment has a criterion at all. The `verification-contract` rule (the rule that checks each criterion's check) used to ask the same question, so its reviewer filed coverage gaps under it. That rule now asks only whether each criterion names a check. On the corrected control document, 9 of 10 panel runs return an empty report, up from 2 of 10. All 10 runs on the defective document still object to the planted criterion.

The `verification-contract` rule (the rule that checks each criterion's check) opened with a sentence that asked the coverage rule's question. It now judges each criterion's check. It sends the question of whether a commitment has a criterion to coverage.
The attack skill's table gains a column that names what each reviewer reads. That unit decides who owns a rule.

The `verification-contract` rule (the rule that checks each criterion's check) used to say every material commitment has a feasible check. That sentence asked the coverage rule's question. The reviewer that owns `verification-contract` filed coverage gaps under it. On the pilot's second case, 18 of 20 runs raised such objections under the rule as it was.

Each attack panel reviewer reads a defined unit. One reads a single criterion's shape. One reads the set against the document's promises. One reads the set against itself. One asks a single criterion what it leaves untested. The unit decides which reviewer owns a rule. Two reviewers may share ground when one asks about a criterion and the other about the set.

The measurement used the pilot's second case, a realistic document with eight criteria and one planted defect, and a corrected control. Ten fresh runs per document read prompts emitted from each version of the standard. Before and after the change, 10 of 10 defective runs objected to the planted criterion under the planted rule. Elsewhere, 1 of 10 defective runs objected, down from 10 of 10. On the control, 9 of 10 runs returned an empty report, up from 2 of 10. The remaining control objection cites a contradiction the test document carries in both versions.

No reviewer prompt changed. No existing attack record is reopened, because the record check binds to the document's revision and never to the rule text. Other sentences in the attack skill were shortened to keep its body under the size cap.
The `verification-contract` rule judges whether each criterion names a feasible and complete check. It sends the question of whether a commitment has a criterion to coverage.

The `verification-contract` rule (the rule that checks each criterion's check) asked the coverage rule's question. Its reviewer filed coverage gaps under it. On the corrected control document, only 2 of 10 runs came back empty.

The `verification-contract` rule (the rule that checks each criterion's check) now judges the check each criterion names. The coverage rule handles whether a commitment has a criterion at all. The attack skill's table names what each reviewer reads. That unit decides who owns a rule.
`make ci` exits 0. On the pilot's second case, 9 of 10 control runs returned an empty report. The planted defect drew objections in 10 of 10 runs. One prose review round came back clean.
